tagline: The 'City of Pearls' is famous for the Charminar, Golconda Fort, glittering bazaars and Hyderabadi biryani, plus a fast-growing tech district.
overview: Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana in southern India. It was founded in 1591 by the Qutb Shahi dynasty, and its symbol, the four-arched Charminar, was built that same decade at the centre of the old city.

West of the city, Golconda Fort was once a centre of the diamond trade; famous stones such as the Koh-i-Noor are linked to the region's mines. The Nizams, who later ruled Hyderabad, were among the world's richest people, and their Chowmahalla and Falaknuma palaces can still be visited.

Around the Charminar, Laad Bazaar sells bangles and the city is known for pearls, giving it the nickname City of Pearls. Hyderabadi biryani and haleem are the signature dishes. The modern HITEC City district hosts major tech companies, and Ramoji Film City is one of the world's largest film studio complexes.
